prompt: An Angular admin feature provides a polling service at component scope and opens an overlay that resolves the same service from a different injector. Closing and reopening the feature leaves multiple pollers running and duplicated notifications appear. Diagnose the injector/lifecycle boundary, make one ownership decision, and prove teardown across feature navigation and overlay close/reopen while preserving the public service API. Do not solve by introducing a global singleton unless the required lifetime actually is application-wide.

Confirm Angular version and standalone/module conventions.

Each feature component owns exactly one service instance and active poller. Its overlay resolves that identical instance without re-providing the service; opening, closing, or reopening the overlay does not restart or stop the feature poller. Concurrent feature owners have distinct service instances. Destroying one owner tears down only its poller and surviving overlay exactly once without manually invoking the service destructor.

Run the Angular build and component/router tests. Assert service identity, start/stop counts, and one notification per poll across overlay close/reopen, repeated close, feature A-to-B navigation, concurrent feature instances, final navigation away, and reentry. Assert detached/destroyed overlay views and removed owned hosts after close or owner destruction, no notifications after teardown, zero pollers after final exit, and a fresh single poller on reentry. Verify actual overlay rendering and keyboard close/focus restoration when supported by its public UI.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not subscribe without lifecycle ownership, mutate shared service state invisibly, bypass template type checking, or mix incompatible reactive patterns without a reason.
